newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks up 2.31 pct to six-year high close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks up 2.31 pct to six-year high close.

text.p: Late buying on Taiwan financials and plastics pushed up share prices sharply higher at the close on Wednesday as bullish sentiment overtook the anxieties that triggered Tuesday's correction, brokers said.
The index rallied despite the watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission's public statement urging 20 local securities investment trust firms not to manipulate stocks.
The benchmark index surged as high as 8,663.07 but settled for a gain of 195.19 points or 2.31 percent at 8,655.82.
The close surpassed a 8,526.20 finish of March 18 to mark the index's highest close since 8,922.67 on May 9, 1990.
Turnover was a huge T$198.6 billion (US$7.2 billion), but still short of Tuesday's all time high T$238.9 billion.
Brokers said sentiment was helped by the government's hands-off attitude as neither the central bank nor finance ministry issued any caution over the sizzling turnover levels.
"No government official criticised the record turnover or the recent stock rally, leading investors to believe further rises are all right," said Albert Lin of Golden Securities.
Initially, investors worried that Tuesday's fall in highly volatile, high-volume trade indicated that heavy profit-taking was emerging, brokers said.

"But as the market now has far more listed firms, more new local mutual funds have been set up and foreign funds have been allowed in, investors should get used to a daily turnover above T$200 billion," said HSBC James Capel analyst Alex Chen.
Even the watchdog commission took pains to say its warning on manipulation was not intended to cool down the market.

"We simply urged them (mutual fund executives) not to get involved in listed firms' management and not to cooperate with major market players to jointly manipulate stock prices," a commission official told Reuters. "Please don't interpret it as a move to cool down the market."
